author: Michael Larabel
description: The Linux 7.3 kernel is out today for an on-time release of this next stable kernel version...
title: Linux 7.3 Released With Faster I/O Performance, AMD Zen 6 Preparations & More

author: Michael Larabel
description: Intel Trust Domain Extensions (TDX) for confidential computing with VMs has assumed the need to perform cache flushing when transitioning memory between KeyIDs used by the total memory encryption (MKTME) for unique AES encryption keys. But it's turned out to be unneeded and the Linux kernel is working now to reduce the excessive cache flushing...
title: It Turns Out Intel TDX Doesn't Need So Much Cache Flushing

author: Michael Larabel
description: The Linux 7.3 kernel is expected to be released as stable later today and with that version there are many exciting changes and improvements. However, the Linux 7.4 kernel merge window will then open up and there are even more exciting changes expected to be merged for this follow-on kernel cycle. Here is a preview of some of the many exciting feature changes expected for Linux 7.4...
title: Linux 7.4 Features Very Exciting With Radeon HDMI 2.1 By Default, AMD PerfOpt, Apple M4

author: Michael Larabel
description: Omarchy 4.0.5 released this weekend as the newest version of this Arch Linux based distribution built around the Hyprland desktop. Omarchy 4.0.5 pulls in the latest Linux 7.2 stable kernel with BORE scheduler, updates against the Qt 6.12 toolkit, and a variety of smaller improvements...
title: Omarchy Gets The Web Browser Launching Faster By Avoiding XDG Overhead

author: Michael Larabel
description: Servo's August status report has finally appeared for outlining progress made on this open-source, Rust-based browser engine. This follows the recent release of the Servo 0.6 software, including the Servoshell demo browser...
title: Servo Gets CSS Grid Working, Threadboost Offering Big Speed-Ups
